## ActingUser

*class*

The logged-in user on whose behalf the PHP front end calls: the id in the X-Acting-User header, believed only on
a request that carries the internal token (the PHP owns the session and is the only one that can say who is logged in);
without a configured token (never in production) it is taken as it comes.

```mermaid

    }

        <<spring>>
    }
    api_ActingUser ..> api_InternalTokenFilter
```

| Member | Visibility | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `int require(HttpServletRequest request, InternalTokenFilter token)` | package static | The acting user's id; a missing, malformed or untrusted header is a BadRequestException (a bug in the caller). |

## ApiExceptionHandler

*class · error handler*

Turns exceptions into JSON error responses with sensible status codes.
The services report failures as plain RuntimeExceptions wrapping the SQLException,
so a constraint violation (foreign key, unique, primary key) is recognised from the cause
and reported as 409 instead of a generic 500.
Every error carries a stable machine-readable code (NOT_FOUND, PAST_DAY, LIST_COMPLETED, ...) next to the
English message, so a client can show its own text without matching message strings.

```mermaid
classDiagram
    direction LR
    class api_ApiExceptionHandler["ApiExceptionHandler"] {
        -Logger log$
        +notFound(NotFoundException e) ResponseEntity~ErrorResponse~
        +pastDay(PastDayException e) ResponseEntity~ErrorResponse~
        +listCompleted(ListCompletedException e) ResponseEntity~ErrorResponse~
        +unauthorized(UnauthorizedException e) ResponseEntity~ErrorResponse~
        +invalidBarcode(InvalidBarcodeException e) ResponseEntity~ErrorResponse~
        +noHousehold(NoHouseholdException e) ResponseEntity~ErrorResponse~
        +notAdmin(NotAdminException e) ResponseEntity~ErrorResponse~
        +invalidInvitation(InvalidInvitationException e) ResponseEntity~ErrorResponse~
        +cannotRemoveSelf(CannotRemoveSelfException e) ResponseEntity~ErrorResponse~
        +invitationLimit(InvitationLimitException e) ResponseEntity~ErrorResponse~
        +emailTaken(EmailTakenException e) ResponseEntity~ErrorResponse~
        +invalidCredentials(InvalidCredentialsException e) ResponseEntity~ErrorResponse~
        +tooManyAttempts(TooManyAttemptsException e) ResponseEntity~ErrorResponse~
        +intakeConflict(IntakeConflictException e) ResponseEntity~ErrorResponse~
        +unknownStore(UnknownStoreException e) ResponseEntity~ErrorResponse~
        +unknownBrand(UnknownBrandException e) ResponseEntity~ErrorResponse~
        +packUnit(PackUnitException e) ResponseEntity~ErrorResponse~
        +pastShoppingDay(PastShoppingDayException e) ResponseEntity~ErrorResponse~
        +badRequest(RuntimeException e) ResponseEntity~ErrorResponse~
        +missingParameter(MissingServletRequestParameterException e) ResponseEntity~ErrorResponse~
        +typeMismatch(MethodArgumentTypeMismatchException e) ResponseEntity~ErrorResponse~
        +unreadableBody(HttpMessageNotReadableException e) ResponseEntity~ErrorResponse~
        +unexpected(RuntimeException e) ResponseEntity~ErrorResponse~
    }
    class api_ErrorResponse["ErrorResponse"] {
        <<record>>
    }
    class api_NotFoundException["NotFoundException"]
    class mealplanner_PastDayException["PastDayException"]
    class shopping_ListCompletedException["ListCompletedException"]
    class api_UnauthorizedException["UnauthorizedException"]
    class barcode_InvalidBarcodeException["InvalidBarcodeException"]
    class api_NoHouseholdException["NoHouseholdException"]
    class api_NotAdminException["NotAdminException"]
    class auth_InvalidInvitationException["InvalidInvitationException"]
    class api_CannotRemoveSelfException["CannotRemoveSelfException"]
    class auth_InvitationLimitException["InvitationLimitException"]
    class auth_EmailTakenException["EmailTakenException"]
    class auth_InvalidCredentialsException["InvalidCredentialsException"]
    class auth_TooManyAttemptsException["TooManyAttemptsException"]
    class barcode_IntakeConflictException["IntakeConflictException"]
    class stores_UnknownStoreException["UnknownStoreException"]
    api_ApiExceptionHandler ..> api_ErrorResponse
    api_ApiExceptionHandler ..> api_NotFoundException
    api_ApiExceptionHandler ..> mealplanner_PastDayException
    api_ApiExceptionHandler ..> shopping_ListCompletedException
    api_ApiExceptionHandler ..> api_UnauthorizedException
    api_ApiExceptionHandler ..> barcode_InvalidBarcodeException
    api_ApiExceptionHandler ..> api_NoHouseholdException
    api_ApiExceptionHandler ..> api_NotAdminException
    api_ApiExceptionHandler ..> auth_InvalidInvitationException
    api_ApiExceptionHandler ..> api_CannotRemoveSelfException
    api_ApiExceptionHandler ..> auth_InvitationLimitException
    api_ApiExceptionHandler ..> auth_EmailTakenException
    api_ApiExceptionHandler ..> auth_InvalidCredentialsException
    api_ApiExceptionHandler ..> auth_TooManyAttemptsException
    api_ApiExceptionHandler ..> barcode_IntakeConflictException

    %% 3 more neighbours not drawn
```

## AssignBarcodeRequest

*record*

Body of PUT /api/barcodes/{code}: what the barcode is. inventoryItemId (the catalogue item), packSize
and packUnit (500 g, 1 kg, 1,5 l, 6 stück) are required; the pack is stored in g, ml or stück like a store
item (1 kg becomes 1000 g, 1,5 l is sent as 1.5 l or 1500 ml) and must fit the item's unit (else 400 PACK_UNIT_MISMATCH); brand (blank or missing =
no brand), name (as printed) and storeItemId (also link the store item that carries it, which must be
for the same catalogue item) are optional. The brand must be an existing one (GET /api/brands); createBrand: true is needed to add a new brand, so a typo cannot create a bogus one (400 UNKNOWN_BRAND).

```mermaid
        +Integer storeItemId
        +Boolean createBrand
    }

        <<controller>>
    }
    api_BarcodeController ..> api_AssignBarcodeRequest
```

## AuditFilter

*class · Spring component · extends OncePerRequestFilter*

Writes the audit line (see AuditLog) for every request, on any path, that is a write or was refused with 401 /
403. It runs before Spring Security, so refused requests (a wrong token) are seen too. The verify endpoint logs its own
line with the typed email. The path is not used to decide what to log (the raw path can be percent-encoded).

```mermaid
classDiagram
    direction LR
    class api_AuditFilter["AuditFilter"] {
        <<spring>>
        -Set~String~ READS$
        -InternalTokenFilter token
        +AuditFilter(InternalTokenFilter token)
        #shouldNotFilter(HttpServletRequest request) boolean
        #doFilterInternal(HttpServletRequest request, HttpServletResponse response, FilterChain chain) void
        ~ipOf(HttpServletRequest request, boolean tokenValid) String$
    }
    class api_InternalTokenFilter["InternalTokenFilter"] {
        <<spring>>
    }
    api_AuditFilter --> api_InternalTokenFilter
```

| Field | Type |
|---|---|
| `READS` | `Set<String>` |
| `token` | `InternalTokenFilter` |

| Member | Visibility | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `AuditFilter(InternalTokenFilter token)` | public |  |
| `boolean shouldNotFilter(HttpServletRequest request)` | protected | The verify endpoint writes its own audit line (with the typed email); decided on the decoded path. |
| `void doFilterInternal(HttpServletRequest request, HttpServletResponse response, FilterChain chain)` | protected |  |
| `String ipOf(HttpServletRequest request, boolean tokenValid)` | package static | The client address for a request (see AuditLog.clientIp). |

## AuditLog

*class*

The audit trail: one line per login, failed login, write and refused request, in the logger "audit", with the client
IP the PHP front end passes on. Never a request body, a query string, a password or a token.

```mermaid
classDiagram
    direction LR
    class api_AuditLog["AuditLog"] {
        -Logger LOG$
        -Pattern IP_LITERAL$
        -Pattern EMAIL_SHAPE$
        +String CLIENT_IP_HEADER$
        +String ACTING_USER_HEADER$
        -Pattern USER_ID$
        ~clientIp(String headerValue, String remoteAddr, boolean tokenValid) String$
        ~actingUser(String headerValue, boolean tokenValid) String$
        ~clean(String value, int max) String$
        +request(String method, String path, int status, String caller, String ip, String user) void$
        +login(boolean success, String typedEmail, String ip) void$
    }
```

| Field | Type |
|---|---|
| `LOG` | `Logger` |
| `IP_LITERAL` | `Pattern` |
| `EMAIL_SHAPE` | `Pattern` |
| `CLIENT_IP_HEADER` | `String` |
| `ACTING_USER_HEADER` | `String` |
| `USER_ID` | `Pattern` |

| Member | Visibility | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `String clientIp(String headerValue, String remoteAddr, boolean tokenValid)` | package static | The client address to log. |
| `String actingUser(String headerValue, boolean tokenValid)` | package static | The acting user id for the log: the header, but only with the internal token and only a plain number; else "-". |
| `String clean(String value, int max)` | package static | Takes anything that could break a log line out of a value and shortens it. |
| `void request(String method, String path, int status, String caller, String ip, String user)` | public static | A request worth keeping: a write, or any request that was refused (401 / 403). |
| `void login(boolean success, String typedEmail, String ip)` | public static | A login attempt. |

## DahaemApplication

*class · command-line tool*

Entry point for the REST API. A thin web layer over the existing services: controllers
translate HTTP to service calls and service results to DTOs, nothing more.
The console runners (StoreImportRunner, ReceiptImportRunner, ...) stay separate entry points.

The database is MariaDB, configured from the DAHAEM_DB_URL, DAHAEM_DB_USER
and DAHAEM_DB_PASSWORD environment variables (see de.dahaem.shared.Database).

## DietDto

*record*

What the diet rules say about a recipe, present only when rules were passed.
status: OK, ANPASSBAR (excluded only through POSSIBLE animals of generic items: see hints),
UNCLEAR (a line of the recipe was not matched and a hard rule applies; only returned with includeUnclear) or
HIDDEN (excluded; returned only by GET /api/recipes/{id}, never in the list).
hints: per item that may come from an excluded animal, the animals it may still be (allowedAnimals,
e.g. Salami → Rind, Geflügel). softHits: what a soft rule (avoidTags / avoidItems) matched; absent when nothing.
unmatchedIngredients: the recipe's lines without a catalogue item (detail only).
Presets filter INGREDIENTS only; this is not a halal or kosher certification.

```mermaid

    direction LR

    }

    }

    }
```

## ErrorResponse

*record*

JSON body for every error response: the HTTP status, its reason phrase, a readable (English) message and a stable
machine-readable code (for example NOT_FOUND, BAD_REQUEST, PAST_DAY, EMAIL_TAKEN, REQUEST_IN_PROGRESS, REQUEST_ID_REUSED, PAST_SHOPPING_DAY, INVALID_BARCODE, BARCODE_CHECKSUM, PACK_UNIT_MISMATCH, UNKNOWN_STORE, UNKNOWN_BRAND, LIST_COMPLETED, CONFLICT, LOGIN_REQUIRED,
CSRF_INVALID, NO_HOUSEHOLD, BAD_CREDENTIALS, TOO_MANY_ATTEMPTS, INVALID_TOKEN) that a client can map to its own text.

## InternalTokenFilter

*class · Spring component · extends OncePerRequestFilter*

Shared-secret gate for the internal API. When INTERNAL_API_TOKEN is set (property
dahaem.internal-token), EVERY request, whatever its path, must carry it in the
X-Internal-Token header: a missing or wrong token is answered with 401 and goes no
further. A request with the right token counts as authenticated (it is the PHP front end, which
owns the user login) and is exempt from CSRF, which only protects browser sessions.

When no token is configured the filter does nothing and nobody is authenticated (the API starts without a token
only for local development and tests, see StartupGuard).

```mermaid
classDiagram
    direction LR
    class api_InternalTokenFilter["InternalTokenFilter"] {
        <<spring>>
        +String HEADER$
        -byte[] expected
        -ObjectMapper objectMapper
        +InternalTokenFilter(String token, ObjectMapper objectMapper)
        +isConfigured() boolean
        +hasValidToken(HttpServletRequest request) boolean
        #shouldNotFilter(HttpServletRequest request) boolean
        #doFilterInternal(HttpServletRequest request, HttpServletResponse response, FilterChain chain) void
    }
    class api_AccountController["AccountController"] {
        <<controller>>
    }
    class api_AuditFilter["AuditFilter"] {
        <<spring>>
    }
    class api_AuthController["AuthController"] {
        <<controller>>
    }
    class api_CallerArgumentResolver["CallerArgumentResolver"] {
        <<spring>>
    }
    class api_InvitationController["InvitationController"] {
        <<controller>>
    }
    class api_ActingUser["ActingUser"]
    class api_SecurityConfig["SecurityConfig"] {
        <<spring>>
    }
    api_AccountController --> api_InternalTokenFilter
    api_ActingUser ..> api_InternalTokenFilter
    api_AuditFilter --> api_InternalTokenFilter
    api_AuthController --> api_InternalTokenFilter
    api_CallerArgumentResolver --> api_InternalTokenFilter
    api_InvitationController --> api_InternalTokenFilter
    api_SecurityConfig ..> api_InternalTokenFilter
```

| Field | Type |
|---|---|
| `HEADER` | `String` |
| `expected` | `byte[]` |
| `objectMapper` | `ObjectMapper` |

| Member | Visibility | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `InternalTokenFilter(String token, ObjectMapper objectMapper)` | public |  |
| `boolean isConfigured()` | public | True if a token is configured (always, in production: see StartupGuard). |
| `boolean hasValidToken(HttpServletRequest request)` | public | True if the request carries the configured token (never true when none is configured). |
| `boolean shouldNotFilter(HttpServletRequest request)` | protected |  |
| `void doFilterInternal(HttpServletRequest request, HttpServletResponse response, FilterChain chain)` | protected |  |

**Referenced by:** `AccountController`, `ActingUser`, `AuditFilter`, `AuthController`, `CallerArgumentResolver`, `InvitationController`, `SecurityConfig`

## InvitationController

*class · REST controller*

Invitations into a household ("Konto erstellen"). An admin of the household makes an invitation and gets its code ONCE;
whoever enters the code on the sign-up page gets an account as a MEMBER of that household. There is no open sign-up.

## PantryIngredientDto

*record*

One ingredient of a suggested recipe. status is IN_STOCK, EXPIRING (in stock and expires
within the look-ahead), EXPIRED (some is in stock but its date has passed: shown with the amount and the
date, not counted as usable stock), MISSING or TO_TASTE. neededQuantity / neededUnit is what
the recipe asks for (quantity null for "to taste"); stockQuantity / stockUnit is what the household
has, in the item's own unit; expiresOn is the earliest expiry date of the stock (null when unknown).
offers lists, for a missing or expired ingredient, every offer that is on sale today (see PantryOfferDto);

## PersistedShoppingListDto

*record*

A previously generated shopping list as it was persisted: its items with names, the amount still needed and its
unit, every current store option for each item (cheapest till price first, but not pre-picked) and the store item
the user has selected, if any. DAHÄM surfaces the options; it never chooses one for the user.

shoppingDate is the day of the trip the list was made for: the offers in the store options are the ones
that run on that day (validFrom / validUntil on each option say when). fromDate is the first
meal day the list counts. Both are null on a list made before they existed.

Each line: available is false when no store currently sells the item (the line is kept, never silently
dropped); needsReview is true when stock exists but in another unit than the line's, so nothing was
subtracted and a person checks it (stockQuantity / stockUnit show what the household has);
recipes are the recipes that need the line; purchased is the tick "bought" on the trip.

archived true = hidden from the overview (nothing is deleted); a free-text line (added with a name)
has no inventoryItemId, its text is in nameDeutsch and nameEnglish, and it has no store options.

status true = completed (read-only). storeTotals: for each store that sells something on the list,
how many of the lines still to buy it covers and what those lines cost there (the cheapest pack option per line);
shown side by side, never picked for the user.

## PlannedMealController

*class · REST controller*

The meal planner by date: read a week, plan a recipe on a day (as often as wanted), edit or move a planned meal,
remove it, and set a recipe's preferred servings. Every meal is addressed by its own entryId. A plan is
one Monday-to-Sunday week; the first meal added to a week creates its plan, so a page never has to create one.

Everything here is the household of the logged-in user (X-Acting-User): its week, its meals, and its head
count for the servings. A meal of another household is a 404. A meal that has no number of its own, no recipe
preference and a household without a head count is cooked for 2.

## RecipeCardDto

*record*

A recipe as a card in the list: what a card shows, nothing more (GET /api/recipes/{id} has the rest:
description, nutrition, image source, publish date, ingredients, instructions). totalTime is
prepTime + cookTime in minutes (0 when the recipe has no time). servings is the number of people;
servingsMax is the upper bound of a "3 – 4 Personen" range (servings is then the lower bound),
null otherwise. imageUrl / thumbnailUrl are links the browser loads from their source (null when
the recipe has no image: show a fallback; use the thumbnail in lists). cuisine is one German name,
ratingAvg is 0 - 5 with 2 decimals; both null when unknown. tags are the recipe's tag names (no
group or source: the detail has those), sorted by group then name; empty when it has none.

## RecipeDetailDto

*record*

One recipe with its nutrition, ingredients and ordered instructions, as returned by /api/recipes/{id}.
servingsMax is the upper bound of a "3 – 4 Personen" range (servings is then the
lower bound), null when the recipe is not a range. people is the head count asked for with
?people=N (null when not asked); each ingredient's scaledQuantity is its
quantity scaled to that count, from servings by default or from servingsMax
when basis is "max", and each instruction's scaledInstruction is its step text
with the amounts for that count. basis is the one actually used: "max" only when
it was asked for and the recipe is a range. scalable is false when that servings count is
not positive, in which case nothing is scaled. The enrichment fields (description,
imageUrl, thumbnailUrl, imageSource, cuisine, ratingAvg,
ratingCount, publishedDate) are as in RecipeSummaryDto; null when missing. tags are the recipe's tags, sorted by group then name:
source is "manual" (added by a person) or "derived" (worked out from DAHÄM's data).
diet is present only when diet rules were passed (see DietDto): the status, the hints and the
recipe's unmatched ingredient lines. householdPreferredServings is the caller's household's permanent
"always for X people" number for this recipe (null when it has none); other households' numbers are never shown.

## ScheduledMealServings

*class*

The nightly job (default 00:01, household time zone): writes the resolved servings onto every meal of a past day
that still follows the default (see MealPlanService.freezePastServings), so history no longer changes when
the household number or a recipe's preference does. It also catches up on any night the API was not running.
Each household is frozen with its own head count. The scheduled method never throws, so a failure cannot stop later runs.

## SecurityConfig

*class · configuration*

Who may call the API: only the PHP front end, which proves it with the shared secret in the X-Internal-Token
header on EVERY request (see InternalTokenFilter). The PHP front end owns the user login and the user session
(POST /api/auth/verify checks a password); the API has no login page, no session login and no static pages.

- /api/** needs the token (or, in tests, a mock user), else 401 as JSON, never a redirect.

- Everything else is denied (the API serves no pages). /error stays open only so that error responses can
      be rendered.

CSRF protection stays on for state-changing requests that do not carry the token; with the token required on every
path none can reach a controller in production. The PHP front end has its own CSRF tokens on its forms.

```mermaid
classDiagram
    direction LR
    class api_SecurityConfig["SecurityConfig"] {
        <<spring>>
        +internalTokenFilterRegistration(InternalTokenFilter filter) FilterRegistrationBean~InternalTokenFilter~
        +passwordEncoder(int strength) PasswordEncoder
        +securityFilterChain(HttpSecurity http, ObjectMapper objectMapper, InternalTokenFilter internalToken) SecurityFilterChain
    }
    class api_InternalTokenFilter["InternalTokenFilter"] {
        <<spring>>
    }
    api_SecurityConfig ..> api_InternalTokenFilter
```

|---|---|---|

| `PasswordEncoder passwordEncoder(int strength)` | public | BCrypt (salted per hash). |
| `SecurityFilterChain securityFilterChain(HttpSecurity http, ObjectMapper objectMapper, InternalTokenFilter internalToken)` | public |  |

## ShoppingListDto

*record*

A shopping list built from recipes: one line per (item, unit), with every current store's option
for it (cheapest till price first, but not pre-picked) and the store item the user has selected,
if any. DAHÄM surfaces the options; it never chooses one for the user.

## ShoppingListDto.StoreOptionDto

*record*

One store's current price for a line: what it costs at the till (sale/deal price where one
applies, plus deposit), plus whether this pack's unit is even comparable to what's needed.
unitCompatible is false when the pack's unit is a different physical dimension (or either
unit is unrecognized) than the line needs; packsNeeded/packsTotalPrice are only ever set
when it's true — never a fabricated pack count for an incompatible unit.

| `PersistedShoppingListDto get(int listId, Caller caller)` | public | Reloads a previously generated/persisted shopping list, with each item's names, options, and selection. |
| `ShoppingListItemSelectionDto selectStoreItem(int listId, int itemId, SelectStoreItemRequest request, Caller caller)` | public | Sets which store product the user picked for a persisted line ({"storeItemId": 5}), or clears the pick ({"storeItemId": null}). |
| `ShoppingListEdits.PurchasedDto setPurchased(int listId, int itemId, ShoppingListEdits.PurchasedRequest request, Caller caller)` | public | Ticks a line as bought on the shopping trip ({"purchased": true}) or unticks it. |
| `ShoppingListEdits.QuantityDto setQuantity(int listId, int itemId, ShoppingListEdits.QuantityRequest request, Caller caller)` | public | Changes the amount of a line ({"quantity": 2.5}, above 0); the unit stays. |
| `void removeItem(int listId, int itemId, Caller caller)` | public | Removes a line from a list that is not completed. |
| `ShoppingListEdits.AddedLineDto addItem(int listId, ShoppingListEdits.AddLineRequest request, Caller caller)` | public | Adds a line by hand: for a catalogue item ({"inventoryItemId": 5, "quantity": 2, "unit": "kg"}, unit optional) or as free text ({"name": "Backpapier", "quantity": 1}, unit optional). |
| `ShoppingListEdits.ArchivedDto setArchived(int listId, ShoppingListEdits.ArchivedRequest request, Caller caller)` | public | Archives a list ({"archived": true}: hidden from the overview, nothing is deleted) or brings it back. |
| `ShoppingListEdits.StatusDto setStatus(int listId, ShoppingListEdits.StatusRequest request, Caller caller)` | public | Completes a list ({"completed": true}: it becomes read-only) or reopens it. |

## StartupGuard

*class · Spring component*

Fail closed: the API does not start without its secrets. A missing or blank INTERNAL_API_TOKEN would leave
only the session login in front of the data, and missing database settings would only show up as errors on the first
request, so both stop the start-up with a message that names the variables (never their values).

For local development only, -Ddahaem.require-secrets=false switches the check off (the tests do this
through src/test/resources/config/application.properties). It is never off by default.

```mermaid
classDiagram
    direction LR
    class api_StartupGuard["StartupGuard"] {
        <<spring>>
        -Logger log$
        ~String TOKEN_ENV$
        ~int RECOMMENDED_TOKEN_LENGTH$
        +StartupGuard(boolean required, String token)
        ~check(boolean required, String token, UnaryOperator~String~ env) void$
    }
```

| Field | Type |
|---|---|
| `log` | `Logger` |
| `TOKEN_ENV` | `String` |
| `RECOMMENDED_TOKEN_LENGTH` | `int` |

| Member | Visibility | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `StartupGuard(boolean required, String token)` | public |  |
| `void check(boolean required, String token, UnaryOperator<String> env)` | package static | Throws if a required secret is missing or blank. |
